title: Construction Social Media Competitive Landscape
summary: Competitive research to sharpen AOM's $3k/month social media retainer pitch for construction.
content:
Construction Social Media -- Competitive Landscape

Research date: 2026-03-08 Purpose: Sharpen AOM's $3k/month retainer pitch for the 15-client / $540k play

What Others Charge

Tier Price Range Who's Offering It What You Get
Budget / DIY-assist $99-$500/mo Smarcomms, Socinova, template-based shops Scheduled posts from stock/client-supplied photos. No strategy. No filming. Basically a posting bot.
Basic agency $500-$1,500/mo Small digital agencies, freelancers 3-5 posts/week, basic graphics, monthly report. One platform focus. No video production.
Mid-tier (where AOM sits) $1,500-$3,500/mo Regional agencies, niche construction marketers Daily posting, custom graphics + some video, 2-3 platforms, bi-weekly reporting, dedicated account manager.
Premium / full-service $3,500-$10,000/mo Thrive, Blue Corona, CyberOptik, larger agencies Multi-platform, professional content creation, paid ad management, influencer outreach, weekly strategy calls.

Key insight: Most agencies in the $1,500-$3,500 range do NOT include on-site filming. They rely on stock photos, client-supplied iPhone pics, or basic Canva graphics. That's the gap.

Typical Package Breakdown

What a standard $2,000-$3,000/mo construction social media package includes:

  • Posts: 12-20 posts/month (3-5/week)
  • Platforms: 2-3 (usually Instagram + Facebook + LinkedIn)
  • Content types: Static graphics, basic reels from client-supplied footage, text posts, occasional carousels
  • Strategy: Initial consultation, monthly content calendar
  • Community management: Basic comment monitoring, not proactive engagement
  • Reporting: Monthly analytics report (reach, engagement, follower growth)
  • Ad spend: Usually NOT included. Managed as separate line item.
  • Video production: Almost never included at this price point
  • On-site visits: Zero

What's conspicuously absent from most packages:

  • Professional on-site filming (drone, gimbal, cinematic quality)
  • Real content from real job sites (most agencies never visit the site)
  • Short-form video editing optimized for Reels/TikTok
  • Employee spotlight and recruitment content
  • AI-assisted content workflows (scheduling, analytics, trend identification)

Where AOM Differentiates

This is the core pitch. Most agencies selling to construction companies are marketing shops that happen to serve contractors. AOM is a production company that happens to do social media. The difference:

1. Real footage from real job sites

  • 83% of contractors fail at social media (CyberOptik stat). The #1 reason: the content looks fake or generic.
  • Real photos outperform stock by 35% in conversion (MarketingExperiments study).
  • User-generated / authentic content gets 28% higher engagement than polished corporate posts.
  • AOM shows up on site. Drone shots. Gimbal walks. Time-lapses. The stuff that actually stops the scroll.

2. Production quality without production prices

  • At $3k/month, most agencies give you Canva templates. AOM gives you cinematic content from a team that shoots $9k corporate videos and documentaries.
  • Same cameras, same crew, same edit quality. Just packaged as a retainer instead of a one-off.

3. AI-powered workflow = more output, less overhead

  • Content calendar generation, caption writing, trend analysis, scheduling, reporting. AI handles the repetitive work.
  • This means AOM can deliver premium content volume at mid-tier prices without burning out.
  • No other construction social media agency is talking about AI workflows. This is white space.

4. Vertical expertise (not just "we serve everyone")

  • AOM is building a construction-specific playbook. Content pillars, posting cadences, hashtag strategies, audience targeting all tuned for contractors.
  • Ambition Mechanical is the proof of concept. KOHRS is the second data point. By client #3, AOM has a repeatable system.

5. Recruitment content built in

  • PCL Construction gets 25% of their engagement from recruitment-focused posts.
  • Construction companies need workers as much as they need clients. Most social media agencies ignore this entirely.
  • AOM can build recruitment into the content mix. Job site culture videos, "day in the life" shorts, crew spotlights.

Strong Construction Social Examples

Company/Account Platform Followers What They Do Well
Kruger Construction (@krugerconstruction) TikTok/IG 3.1M Family man + contractor brand. Personality-driven. Shows the human side of construction. Massive reach.
Eddy Lopez (@ez_home) TikTok 2.6M Washington state contractor. Real job site footage with engaging audio. Proves a local contractor can build a massive audience.
PCL Construction LinkedIn/IG 410K (LI), 26K (IG) North America's largest contractor. 25% of content is recruitment-focused. Professional but approachable. Proof that B2B construction content works on LinkedIn.
Ken White Construction TikTok/IG Growing Real job site footage with trending audio on TikTok. Instagram mixes podcast clips, equipment spotlights, employee features, and step-by-step job walkthroughs. Textbook multi-format strategy.
NS Builders (@nsbuilders, Nick Schiffer) IG/YouTube 300K+ High-end residential. Beautiful project photography + behind-the-scenes process content. Shows that quality attracts quality clients.

Pattern: The winners all share one thing: real footage from real sites with real people. Nobody blowing up on construction social media is using stock photos.

Top Performing Content Types

Instagram

  • Reels: Construction sector led ALL industries on Instagram Reels in Jan 2025 with 2.6% average engagement rate. Time-lapses, before/after reveals, and "satisfying work" clips dominate.
  • Carousels: Project walkthroughs (swipe through the build process). Educational content (5 things to know before hiring a contractor).
  • Stories: Day-in-the-life, crew spotlights, poll/quiz engagement, job site updates.

TikTok

  • POV clips: "POV: When the GC says it'll only take an hour." Relatable humor + real footage = viral potential.
  • Time-lapses: Scaffold setup, demolition, full build compressed into 30 seconds.
  • Trending audio + job site footage: The audio is the hook. The footage is the proof.
  • Before/after reveals: Highest save rate. People share these.

LinkedIn

  • Carousels and photos outperform video on LinkedIn (different algorithm).
  • Project case studies: Commercial clients and industry peers live here.
  • Recruitment posts: "We're hiring" + crew culture content. Construction LinkedIn is hungry for this.
  • Thought leadership: Safety practices, sustainability, industry trends.

Cross-platform truth: Short-form vertical video is king across all three platforms. But the format changes: TikTok wants personality and humor, Instagram wants visual polish, LinkedIn wants professional credibility.

AOM's $3k/month Package Recommendation

Based on this research, here's what AOM's $3k/month retainer should include to sit above the competition while staying profitable:

"The Jobsite" -- $3,000/month

Content Production:

  • 1 on-site filming session per month (half-day, 3-4 hours)
  • Drone + gimbal + cinematic camera setup
  • 16-20 posts/month across all platforms
  • 8-10 short-form videos (Reels/TikTok) per month from real footage
  • 4-6 static posts (project photos, graphics, carousels)
  • 2-4 Story sets per month

Platforms: Instagram + TikTok + LinkedIn (3 platforms)

Strategy & Management:

  • Custom content calendar (monthly)
  • AI-assisted caption writing and hashtag optimization
  • Community management (comments, DMs, engagement)
  • Monthly analytics report with actionable insights
  • Quarterly strategy review call

What makes this worth $3k (when others charge $3k for Canva templates):

  • Real cinematic footage from YOUR job sites, not stock
  • The same production team that shoots $9k corporate videos
  • AI workflow means higher output without higher cost
  • Content that works for both client acquisition AND recruitment

Upsell Path

  • $3,500/month: Add paid ad management (client covers ad spend separately)
  • $4,500/month: Add 2 filming sessions per month + dedicated recruitment content track
  • Website add-on: $3-5k one-time (the Ambition Mechanical play)
  • Brand video: $5-9k one-time project upsell after 3+ months on retainer

Why $3k is the right number

  • Below $2k: Can't include on-site filming. Margins too thin. Competing with template shops.
  • At $3k: Filming is included. Content quality is undeniable. AOM is differentiated. Margin supports 1 hire at 10+ clients.
  • Above $4k: Harder close for the construction vertical. Save premium pricing for the upsell after proving ROI.

The Pitch in One Line

"Most agencies post for you. We film for you. Real footage from your job sites, edited like the $9k videos we make for corporate clients, delivered as a monthly retainer."

Sources: WebFX, SociallyIn, Sprout Social, Buildertrend, CyberOptik, MarketingExperiments, Modash, Feedspot, CONEXPO-CON/AGG, Projectmark, Buffer, Planable, OpenAsset, Construction Dive
